issues.kind: CATALOGUE (a hand bend whose line no form words)
issues.claim: §7.1's bend.wall.raisedCrossing row (base l. 11339) moves, as part of a hand stretch's bend, 'a gate it makes for a ground way ... moved only as law 2 (a) moves it, to the place law 3 picks' - along that way (law 3, l. 2849: 'a gate the op's own wall lays on a standing way, along that way'; the bent-group sentence (iv), l. 3207-3210; W2's last column, l. 3339) - and T110-2 (4) runs it twice (l. 19416-19422, the aqueduct's margin case; l. 19440-19441, the viaduct case), each naming bend.wall.raisedCrossing. V09's line for that key (V09 l. 2104) takes 'its form by what was drawn or moved', and none of its seven forms is this move: the gate form is 'for a gate dropped or slid inside the under-deck strip ... (T3's Gate, a gate's grip)' and says the gate 'moves {m} m along {wall}', where this gate moves along the ground way; the keep-clear, crossing, fixed-place and castle forms name other moves. One builder words it in the gate form, another in the keep-clear or crossing form; the geometry is the laws' in every build and no bar counts lines (VF7w-HND-02's and VF7-HND-03's class).
issues.required_change: V09 §4.9's bend.wall.raisedCrossing (V09 l. 2104), its line cell: after 'and, for a crossing moved along {way} to the nearest lawful one (§2.7's laws, law 1 (2)–(4), law 3; its worked example the bent-group sentence (i)), "The wall crosses {way} {m} m from your line, where it can pass."' insert ' — and, for a gate the stretch makes for a ground way moved along that way to where §2.7's laws admit it (law 1 (5), law 2 (a), law 3; its worked example the bent-group sentence (iv)), "The gate for {road} stands {m} m along it, where a gate can stand; the wall passes through it." — `{road}` the ground way's name, else its class's word'.

issues.kind: READERS (law 2 cited without its order; adjudication-r7x.md's F3, the D6 sweep's residue)
issues.claim: adjudication-r7x.md ruled that every family text naming how an op meeting a raised way resolves it cites 'law 2, in its order' (F3), and D6 so rewrote §7.3's S7 row (l. 11597: 'the meeting by §2.7's laws (law 2, in its order ...)'); §4.11 Other crossings reads 'law 2, in its order ... a run with no lawful shape giving way (law 2 (c))' (l. 8961-8963). The water operator's own batch, §7.3 (b) 3 - the step that re-traces a wall run a moved river crosses (by hand moveCourseKnot, drawWater, a follow terrain stroke) - still cites law 2 (a) alone, twice: l. 11692-11694 '(the raised way met by §2.7's laws, law 2 (a); its worked example the crossing table's row W2; §4.11 Other crossings)' and l. 11699-11702 '(never a standing raised way or its reservation, which a re-traced run meets by §2.7's laws, law 2 (a); ...)'. A run with no lawful shape takes law 2 (c) - by hand refuse.raised.meeting, at an epoch the water op waiting (F-REDERIVE's raised-way rung, l. 9869; §7.1's refuse row, l. 11340) - which these citations leave out; the outcome rows give it and §5.3's row catches any other build, so every build keeps law 1.
issues.required_change: §7.3 (b) 3: (1) (l. 11692-11694) '(the raised way met by §2.7's laws, law 2 (a); its worked example the crossing table's row W2; §4.11 *Other crossings*)' → '(the raised way met by §2.7's laws, law 2, in its order — a run with no lawful shape taking F-REDERIVE's raised-way rung (§5.2) —; its worked example the crossing table's row W2; §4.11 *Other crossings*)'; (2) (l. 11700-11702) 'which a re-traced run meets by §2.7's laws, law 2 (a); its worked example the crossing table's *beneath*, row W2' → 'which a re-traced run meets by §2.7's laws, law 2, in its order; its worked example the crossing table's *beneath*, row W2'.

issues.kind: READERS (a gate's resolution restated with a trigger missing; F3)
issues.claim: Law 2 Carried way (l. 2790-2792): 'Where the wall is shape-locked, or law 2 (a) leaves the way no lawful gate in it, the carried way ... is re-routed by law 2 (b) ... through the nearest gate of that wall that a way of its class may pass ..., else the op takes law 2 (c)'. §7.1 Raised ways (l. 11145-11149) restates the hand raised road's gate with the first trigger only: 'passes through the gate its ground way makes there — in a placement-locked wall too, the fate reshaped, and in a shape-locked one none, the way re-routed through the nearest gate of that wall ..., else refused (§2.7's laws, law 2 Carried way, law 1 (10), law 4's (G2))'; V09 §4.20.2 (4) (V09 l. 3016-3019) with neither ('passes through the gate the ground way makes there'), and its ground-road clause (V09 l. 3029-3030: 'crosses under the nearest span §4.3 admits, a road no span admits going round it') omits the gate move §7.1's bend.raised.underSpan row (l. 11341) and row (b) (l. 2914) make. Case: a hand raised road whose carried way crosses an unlocked enceinte under a second standing raised way (a viaduct, or an aqueduct whose span there does not clear the gatehouse), so law 1 (5) (l. 2724-2725) bars the gate there; the laws give (a) the crossing moved to the nearest place they admit the gate, else (b) the re-route, else (c). Each text cites Carried way, which decides the case, and a build of the bare words makes a gate §5.3's law-1 row rejects at the commit: an omission of a case the cited law decides (VF7v-EPO-05's grade), one more member of adjudication-r7x.md's class that D3 left in this sentence.
issues.required_change: (1) §7.1 *Raised ways, aqueducts and retaining walls* (l. 11146-11149): 'and passes through the gate its ground way makes there — in a placement-locked wall too, the fate *reshaped*, and in a shape-locked one none, the way re-routed through the nearest gate of that wall a way of its class may pass, else refused (§2.7's laws, law 2 *Carried way*, law 1 (10), law 4's (G2)) —' → 'and passes through the gate its ground way makes there — in a placement-locked wall too, the fate *reshaped* (law 4's (G2)); a gate §2.7's laws bar there, a shape-locked wall's among them, resolved by those laws, law 2, in its order: (a) the way's crossing of the wall moved to the nearest place they admit its gate, (b) else the way re-routed through the nearest gate of that wall a way of its class may pass, (c) else refused (§2.7's laws, law 1 (5), (10), law 2 *Carried way*, law 3) —'. (2) END at V09, §4.20.2 (4): (V09 l. 3017-3019) 'ramps down to a ground vertex before it and passes through the gate the ground way makes there (§2.7's laws, law 1 (3), law 2 *Carried way*; its worked example *down before the wall*; `bend.raised.wall`)' → 'ramps down to a ground vertex before it and passes through the gate the ground way makes there, a gate §2.7's laws bar there (a shape-locked wall's among them) resolved by those laws, law 2, in its order — the crossing moved, else the way re-routed through the nearest gate of that wall, else refused (§2.7's laws, law 1 (3), (5), (10), law 2 *Carried way*; its worked example *down before the wall*; `bend.raised.wall`)'; and (V09 l. 3029-3030) 'crosses under the nearest span §4.3 admits, a road no span admits going round it,' → 'crosses under the nearest span §4.3 admits — its crossing of a wall's trace beneath the deck moved to the nearest at which §2.7's laws admit its gate (law 1 (5), law 2 (a), law 3; its worked example the way-and-channel table's row (b)) —, a road no span admits going round it,'.

held_notes.note: 'it cuts every other way the new channel ⊕ bank setback meets' names no exception for a raised way whose deck passes over a moved river's new channel, where a carve keeps it by the way-and-channel table's row (e) — raised way × water; persisting as adjudication-r7x.md's held note 5.
